$comment: flow: S4 step 7 (the result is committed through commit_outcome as typed proposals, never as agent-written state); S4 steps 3, 6, 8, 9 (screening, provisional capture, verification, accepted support at the commit boundary); §3 step 4 (a decision action commits through the same path); S8 item 1 (the outbox event is committed atomically) | boundaries: Router; Station supervisor; Primary agent (per-station frontier LLM); Verifier; Secondary/delegate agents | design-review: §5 commit_outcome steps 1-4 (the typed outcome document lives in the protected spool, addressed by payload_digest, and is validated outside the write transaction) | invariants: C-2; C-3; C-4; C-7; C-9; C-12; V-4; V-10; RG-5; G-12; P-1; D-2 | note: added by task 1b. The document the router reads, by digest, for one commit. It carries only proposals whose authority the router derives from the committing capability: there is no producer, verifier, recorder, signal-source or role field, because the router fills each of those in from the invocation the capability names. Which sections an invocation kind may carry is the router's rule (gen2/router/boundary.py SECTION_KINDS), not this schema's
title: commit_outcome outcome document
description: Staged by trusted station code in the protected spool and named by the commit envelope's payload_digest (the bytes are hashed exactly as staged). Every section is present, empty when unused, so a missing section is a malformed document rather than a silent default. Identity fields repeat the envelope's so the document cannot be replayed under another invocation, topic or operation kind.

next_queue_state.description: A research pass's proposal for its topic when its final outcome releases the lease: rest or requeue. The router applies it only to an active topic (gen2/store/README.md queue table: active -> resting / queued, router). Null otherwise.

claims.description: Provisional capture (flow S4 step 6). The producer of each revision is the committing invocation, never a field here (INVARIANTS V-10: production and adoption are bound to the commit and its receipt). Adopting a scoping claim is writing its next revision.

claim_promotions.description: Claim revisions of the committing invocation's topic proposed for accepted support; the store's V-4 and V-10 gates decide.

verification_receipts.description: Committed only by the verification invocation the receipt names as its verifier, under that invocation's own capability (RG-5).

decision_receipts.description: Receipts of decision-provider calls made inside the committing invocation (flow §3 step 4).

screening_assessments.description: Unit 3 (assessed candidates). The contract revision, framing and eligibility-protocol versions are the committing invocation's pinned revision's, filled in by the router; criterion ids must be that protocol's.

criterion_results.description: Per criterion of the pinned eligibility protocol: met, not_met, or unknown (missing information is unknown, never an exclusion).

review_triggers.description: Semantic trigger observations of the primary (flow S5). The identity is the router's hash of (topic, reason, cause, source revision), so a replayed trigger collides instead of re-opening; mandatory retraction and decision-record signals are raised by code policy or the operator, never by a commit (G-12).

holds.description: Typed, owned, deadlined holds created open by this commit (H-3).

exports.description: Export manifests committed to the outbox with this commit (P-1; EXPORT-API.md §3). Each is validated against export-manifest/2 and its extension connectors admitted before it is written (EXPORT-API.md §5).

allOf.description: Only a final outcome releases a lease, so only it proposes what the topic does next.
